subject.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk

question: Should this PR remain blocked until the contributor supplies real delete-and-path-reuse output from a current-main-refreshed exact head, or should a maintainer explicitly override that proof gate after performing equivalent validation?
rationale: The deterministic coverage is strong, but the only live output exercises an earlier implementation, and external PR policy requires after-fix real behavior evidence for the exact behavior being merged.

options.title: Require refreshed exact-head proof
options.body: Refresh the patch onto current main and require redacted filesystem or runtime output showing deletion removes both artifacts and reuse preserves the new pair.

options.title: Maintainer proof override
options.body: Allow a maintainer to run and document equivalent exact-head real validation before explicitly overriding the contributor proof requirement.

recommendation.title: Require refreshed exact-head proof
recommendation.body: Refresh the patch onto current main and require redacted filesystem or runtime output showing deletion removes both artifacts and reuse preserves the new pair.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the current assignee and reviewer who defined the lifecycle acceptance condition.
